subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should OpenClaw allow configured model fallback after context-overflow recovery is exhausted, and what replay-safety and context-window constraints should gate it?
rationale: Both directions are product-valid: current docs and code intentionally keep overflow inside compaction/retry, while the issue reports a real long-session recovery gap that changes provider/model routing and session replay semantics.

options.title: Implement guarded larger-window fallback
options.body: Allow fallback only after compaction and truncation fail, only to candidates with known sufficient effective context, and preserve replay-safety and delivery guards.

options.title: Keep compaction-only behavior
options.body: Document that context overflow is not a model-fallback trigger and improve visible recovery guidance instead.

options.title: Defer behind context UX work
options.body: Prioritize diagnostics and model-switch recovery while leaving larger-context fallback as an explicit future policy decision.

recommendation.title: Implement guarded larger-window fallback
recommendation.body: Allow fallback only after compaction and truncation fail, only to candidates with known sufficient effective context, and preserve replay-safety and delivery guards.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of recent central-file history and prior issue-review context for this policy boundary.
